newsitem.title: USA: Companies to spend $800 million to develop oilfield.
newsitem.headline: Companies to spend $800 million to develop oilfield.

text.p: A trio of oil companies that won the right to drill for oil in part of Alaska's North Slope this week said Wednesday they plan to invest up to $800 million in the project.
The Alpine oilfield, located in the Colville River delta, is to start producing 30,000 barrels of oil a day in the year 2000, the companies said.

Atlantic Richfield Co. unit Arco Alaska Inc., Anadarko Petroleum and Union Texas Petroleum won five tracts in the area with bids of about $2 million, preliminary figures from the Alaska Division of Oil and Gas showed.

The companies plan to begin construction and development of the field late next year or early in 1998, pending receipt of local, state and federal permits. Production is expected to double to about 60,000 barrels daily in 2001, they said.

Total field development is expected to cost $700 million to $800 million, the companies said in a statement Wednesday. Arco owns 56 percent of the partnership, with Anadarko and Union Texas each holding 22 percent.

The three oil companies have worked together in the past few years to explore the delta, located about 50 miles west of the trans-Alaska pipeline's northern terminal at Prudhoe Bay. Results of their exploration work has been largely confidential.
